title: How the Heat is Messing with Your Sleep - Nautilus
gist: A Climate Central analysis finds the average person globally lost almost 56 hours of sleep a year to elevated nighttime temperatures from 2020 to 2025, as heat waves spread across the US, North Africa, the Middle East, and Southern Europe.

insights.claim: The average person around the globe lost almost 56 hours of sleep a year to elevated nighttime temperatures from 2020 to 2025, per a Climate Central analysis.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Quantifies a measurable climate-health cost with implications for productivity and cooling demand.
insights.locator: lost almost 56 hours of sleep a year to elevated nighttime temperatures

insights.claim: Heat waves are affecting much of the US Southwest and Southern California as well as North Africa, the Middle East, and Southern Europe, meaning billions may struggle to sleep.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Maps the broad geographic footprint of heat-driven sleep disruption relevant to public health and energy planning.
insights.locator: Heat waves are blazing through much of Southern California

insights.claim: The author reports firsthand that hot, humid nights without air conditioning in San Diego have produced damp sheets and restless, fan-cooled sleep—framing this as possibly the new normal.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Personalizes the systemic finding and hints at rising residential cooling demand.
insights.locator: nights in San Diego where I live have been hot and sticky
